t: A Turkic-ruled, Persianised empire that rose from the Amu Darya oasis of Khwarazm to rule from western Iran to the Syr Darya.
It grew rich on Silk Road trade, but rapid conquests left it with divided commands and loyalties it never resolved.
Killing a Mongol envoy in 1218 brought Genghis Khan's invasion, which destroyed the empire and opened Iran to the Mongols.
dyk: In 1217 Muhammad II marched on Baghdad against the Abbasid caliph, but the campaign was abandoned when snow overwhelmed his army in the Zagros mountains.
ev: Ala ad-Din Tekish comes to power and throws off Seljuk overlordship
Tekish defeats and kills Toghrul III, the last Seljuk sultan of Iraq
Ala ad-Din Muhammad II takes the throne and expands against the Ghurids and Qara Khitai
Muhammad II's march on Baghdad is abandoned in the snows of the Zagros
Otrar's governor massacres a Mongol-sponsored caravan; the shah executes a Mongol envoy
Bukhara and Samarkand fall to Genghis Khan's armies
The empire effectively ceases to exist; Jalal ad-Din is defeated on the Indus
Jalal ad-Din dies after a decade of resistance in Iran and the Caucasus
